english.title: Publish name / address / photograph of sex victim - other publication
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) during the lifetime of **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) when an allegation had been made that an offence, of **(..SPECIFY OFFENCE..) had been committed against

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

and being the publisher of **(..SPECIFY PUBLICATION..), published therein

(C)_[the name]_
(D)_[the address]_
(E)_[a still picture]_
(F)_[a moving picture]_

of **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), being a matter likely to lead members of the public to identify **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) as the person against whom the offence was alleged to have been committed
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) and 5(1) of the Sexual Offences (Amendment) Act 1992.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
during lifetime of victim when allegation had been made
that sexual offence had been committed against victim
being the publisher of publication
published name/address/still picture/moving picture
likely to lead members of the public to identify victim

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The consent of the Attorney General is required for a prosecution.
(ii) For the list of relevant sexual offences to which this offence applies.
(iii) Although section 1 refers to a 'written publication' section 5(1)(b) provides for 'publication in any other form'. 'Written publication' includes a film, a soundtrack and any other record in permanent form (section 6).
(iv) See also offence wording: H4320 - for offence in newspaper or periodical.
(v) See also offence wordings: H4322, H4323 and H4324 which relate to complainants for sex offences (where someone has been accused).

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
